title: Introduction to Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
description: Human communication disorders. Fields of audiology and speech-language pathology. Disability, hearing, language, speech, and communication for participation in society.

title: Sign Languages and Deaf Culture
description: Introduction to sign languages, deafness and deaf culture. General issues of human language, language learning, and minority societies.

title: Communication as a Human Right
description: Human communication disorders and how they influence abilities to engage in various domains of life to include community engagement, education, legal and medical systems, media, and politics.

title: Introduction to Research
description: Research methods and tools that can be applied in a variety of research laboratories.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Introduction to Language Science
description: Structure, acquisition, processing, and neurological organization of language in typical and disordered communication.

title: Hearing Science
description: Concepts of hearing science. Hearing science components to include physical acoustics, anatomy and physiology of auditory system, and psychoacoustics.

title: Phonetics
description: Principles of speech production and practical skills in discriminating and transcribing sounds of various dialects in English and other languages, as well as clinical populations. Competency in IPA broad and narrow transcription, classification of speech sounds, and patterns of speech.

title: Anatomy and Physiology of Speech
description: Anatomy and physiology of respiratory, phonatory, and articulatory systems related to speech.

title: Principles of Audiology
description: Diagnostic audiology procedures: Pure-tone testing, masking, speech recognition testing and immittance. Integration and interpretation of results from the basic audiological test battery.

title: Topics in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
description: Study of some problem in speech, language, and hearing sciences.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Guided Observations
description: Twenty-five hours of guided observations. Clinical activities and debriefing of therapy and evaluation procedures.

title: Aural Rehabilitation
description: Theoretical, methodological, and technical issues related to facilitating receptive and expressive communication in individuals who are deaf or hard-of-hearing. Emphasizes multidisciplinary case management of children.

title: Phonological Acquisition and Disorders
description: Phonology, phonological development, and phonological disorders as they relate to basic linguistic theory. Concepts considered through critical thinking and problem-solving.

title: Foundations of Speech-Language: Development
description: Speech-language development as related to theories of language acquisition, development, and clinical practice in children from birth to school-age.

title: Foundations of Speech-Language: Differences and Disorders in Children
description: Speech and language disorders and issues related to assessment of and intervention with children from culturally and linguistically diverse populations.

title: Speech-Language Screening of Children
description: Screening speech and language of children in various community facilities and settings.

title: Clinical Processes
description: Clinical issues, policies, and methods in speech-language pathology. Experience in writing lesson plans and clinical reports. Clinical observation to partially fulfill requirements for certification.

title: Neuroanatomy and Disorders of Speech and Language
description: Structural and functional neuroanatomy and disorders of speech and language resulting from pathology of the nervous system.

title: Dysphagia
description: Measurement techniques and research in dysphagia. Assessment and treatment of dysphagia and swallowing problems in children and adults.

title: Communication Processes and Aging
description: Normal and disordered communication processes in the aging.

title: Research Practicum
description: Participation in a specific research activity under faculty supervision.

title: Selected Topics in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
description: Specialized study of selected topics from the area of speech-language pathology, audiology, education of the hearing impaired, and speech and hearing science.

title: Research Methods in Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Methods of investigation in communication sciences and disorders to include research design, basic statistics, principles of evidence-based practice, ethical conduct in research design and work with human participants.

title: Advanced Research Methods in Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Principles of evidence-based practice, single-subject design, statistics for single-subject design, statistics used in longitudinal research and scale development; regression and factor analysis.

title: Voice, Resonance, and Fluency Disorders
description: Normal voice, resonance, and fluency, symptoms and causes of voice, resonance, and fluency disorders and their assessment and management.

title: Phonology and Phonological Disorders
description: Characterization of phonological disorders, assessment frameworks, intervention strategies. Theoretical frameworks of phonology as applied to and experimentally evaluated in speech-language pathology. Methodology considered within context of clinical cases studies designed to facilitate critical thinking and problem-solving.

title: Motor Speech Disorders
description: Theories and clinical methods of diagnosis and intervention pertaining to motor speech disorders in children and adults.

title: Acquired Neurogenic Language and Cognitive Disorders I
description: Theories and clinical methods of diagnosis and intervention pertaining to language and communication disorders in adults with left or right hemisphere brain damage.

title: Acquired Neurogenic Language and Cognitive Disorders II
description: Theories and clinical methods of diagnosis and intervention pertaining to cognitive and linguistic disorders in adolescents and adults with traumatic brain injury, dementing illness or frontal lobe impairments.

title: Language Disorders: Infancy Through Preschool
description: Major theories of language development with focus on early language development; effect of theoretical perspective on approaches to assessment and intervention; development and evaluation of assessment and intervention procedures and instruments.

title: Language Disorders: School Age Through Adolescence
description: Normal and impaired language development in children five years through adolescence. Assessment and intervention for language disorders across spoken and written modalities.

title: Diagnostic Methods in Speech-Language Pathology
description: Principles and procedures for culturally relevant assessment of communication disorders in children and adults. Ethnographic interviewing; formal, informal, and unbiased testing; clinical reporting. Practice with selected methods and tools.

title: Diagnostic Practica in Speech-Language Pathology
description: Supervised diagnostic practica with children and adults with a variety of speech-language disorders. Four hours of supervision per week.
notes: Not open to students with credit in SLHS 618A or SLHS 618B.

title: Multidisciplinary Diagnostic Practicum in Speech-Language Pathology
description: Participation in multidisciplinary assessment of infants and toddlers.

title: Clinical Intervention in Speech-Language Pathology
description: Supervised intervention practica with children and adults with a variety of speech-language disorders. Up to four hours per week of client contact plus staffing. Up to three units may be taken concurrently per semester.

title: Neurogenic Speech-Language Intervention
description: Supervised intervention practica with adults with neurogenic communication disorders. Up to four hours per week of client contact plus staffing. Up to three units may be taken concurrently.

title: Voice/Fluency/Dysphagia Clinical Intervention
description: Supervised intervention practica with voice, fluency, and/or swallowing disorders. Up to two hours per week of client contact plus staffing. Up to three units may be taken concurrently.

title: Advanced Field Clinical Practice in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
description: Supervised practice with speech-language-hearing problems in off-campus settings. Up to 10 hours per week of client contact plus staffing. Up to three units may be taken concurrently.

title: Professional Skills in Speech-Language Pathology I
description: Development of professional skills to include client advocacy, ethical and legal decision-making, interpersonal skills for team collaboration, and knowledge of professional policies and procedures.

title: Professional Skills in Speech-Language Pathology II
description: Development of professional skills necessary for working successfully in off-campus settings to include caseload management, conflict resolution, professional credentialing requirements, and supervision/leadership skills.

title: Communication Disorders in Bilingual Adults
description: Linguistic and cognitive system in normal bilingual adults compared to monolingual peers, and in bilingual adults with language disorders. Assessment and intervention strategies in bilingual adults’ communicative and cognitive disorders. Cross-cultural issues in selection of assessment and intervention procedures.

title: Communication Disorders in Bilingual Children
description: Normal and atypical language development applied to assessment and treatment of communication disorders in bilingual and monolingual children. Alternative assessment and intervention methods.

title: Augmentative Communication
description: Alternative and augmentative approaches, strategies and technology for individuals with severe communication impairments. Assessment and intervention. Project required.

title: Selected Topics in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
description: Intensive study in specific areas of audiology, education of hearing impaired, speech and hearing science, and speech-language pathology.

title: Seminar in Neurogenic Communication Disorders
description: Neurogenic communication disorders in children and adults to include aphasia, cognitive-communication disorders, dysarthria, apraxia of speech, and/or dementia. Theoretical frameworks, treatment, management, and intervention of these disorders.

title: Scientific Grant Writing
description: How to write scientific grant proposals, how the grant reviewing process works, and search for available funding opportunities.

title: Seminar in Disorders of Language and Cognition/Children
description: Language impairment in children, including primary versus secondary language impairment, modular versus processing explanations, relationships between language and cognition, as well as disassociations of development across different populations.

title: Seminar in Language Disorders in Multilingual Populations
description: Language disorders in linguistically diverse populations. Disorders of phonological, morphological, syntactic, and semantic aspects of target languages and their clinical implications.

title: Advanced Research Practicum
description: Participation in a specific research activity under faculty supervision

title: Research
description: Research in speech-language pathology, deaf education or audiology.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Thesis or Project
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis or Project Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis or project is granted final approval.

title: Comprehensive Examination Extension
description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master’s degree Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.

title: Seminar in Foundations of Language Science
description: Current issues, theory, and research concerning language representation, processing, and neurological organization in adults.

title: Advanced Seminar in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
description: Critical evaluation of theoretical frameworks, synthesis of interdisciplinary knowledge, and translation of theory to research methodology in speech, language, and hearing sciences.

title: Doctoral Research
description: Individual investigation to the general field of the dissertation.

title: Doctoral Special Study
description: Individual study in the field of specialization.

title: Doctoral Dissertation
description: Preparation of the dissertation for the doctoral degree. Enrollment is required during the term in which the dissertation is approved.

title: Clinical Practice in Public Schools
description: Clinical practice in elementary or secondary schools or community colleges in speech-language pathology. Applies only toward Clinical-Rehabilitative Services Credential (C-RS) or Certificate of Clinical Competency in Speech-Language Pathology (ASHA).
